title: Two white cloths
hook: men wear two unstitched white cloths; women wear modest ordinary clothes

segments.voice: Yesterday, the miqat, and your line: the boundary. Which threshold did you cross with a little more attention? Day one thousand one hundred twenty-two.

Two pieces of white cloth. No seams, no buttons, no collar, no label. One is wrapped around the waist. The other goes over the shoulders. That's the whole outfit. A pilgrim reaches the boundary from yesterday, takes off the clothes that said who he was at home, the suit or the uniform or the team jersey, and puts these on. The man next to him does the same. So does the man next to him. Within an hour, you can't tell the surgeon from the taxi driver. Today, the word for what has just happened to them.
screen: `NO SEAMS, NO LABEL.` → `THE CLOTHES FROM HOME COME OFF.` → `NOBODY CAN TELL WHO IS WHO.`

segments.voice: First, the word. Ihram is not really the name of the cloth. It's the name of a state the pilgrim enters, at the boundary, with an intention. The two cloths are how that state looks from the outside, and people call them the ihram too. Second, how the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ described it. Someone asked him what a person in ihram should wear. The report is in Sahih al-Bukhari, and his answer is a surprise: he didn't describe the outfit. He listed what to leave off. No shirts, no turbans, no trousers, no hooded cloaks, no leather socks. The clothes are defined by what's missing. Whatever is cut and sewn to the shape of a body, with its fashion and its rank, stays home. Third, the women. A woman in ihram doesn't wrap herself in two white cloths. She wears her own ordinary, modest clothes, and another report in Bukhari says she doesn't wear a face veil or gloves in that state. So the rule isn't one uniform for everybody. It's simplicity for everybody, in the shape that fits. Fourth, what it does. Put a crowd of people from everywhere into the same plain dress, and the usual signals go quiet. Nobody's watch is on show. Nobody's accent shows in the cut of a coat. Some pilgrims say the two white cloths remind them of a shroud, plain cloth like the cloth Muslims are buried in, and that thought travels with them for the whole journey. Whether or not that's what the cloth means to a given pilgrim, the effect is the same. For a few days, the person inside the cloth is just a person, standing among people, dressed alike.
screen: `A STATE, NOT JUST A CLOTH.` · `DEFINED BY WHAT'S LEFT OFF.` · `WOMEN: THEIR OWN MODEST CLOTHES.` · `THE SIGNALS GO QUIET.`

segments.voice: The practice: wear something plain. It can be now or later today. Take off one thing you wear partly so people will notice it, a logo, a watch, a piece of jewelry that says something about you, and set it aside. Then settle, and breathe. Notice whether you feel any lighter, or any barer. If you pray, you can sit with the picture of the pilgrims in their plain cloth and say a verse you know. If you don't, just stay with the breath, and with being nobody in particular for two minutes. The bell holds the time.
Ihram. The sacred state a pilgrim enters at the boundary, and the plain clothes that show it. Today's word.
Your line: all dressed alike. Today, when you meet someone, notice the first thing you read from their clothes, and then look past it. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Men entering ihram for Hajj or Umrah put on two unstitched white cloths, one around the waist and one over the shoulders; women wear their own modest clothes. Pilgrims make their intention at the miqat and stay in ihram until the rites release them.

notes: Bukhari 1542 (Ibn Umar: what the muhrim may not wear: shirts, turbans, trousers, hooded cloaks, khuffs): confirm number and the list. The hadith also mentions saffron- or wars-dyed garments and an exception for khuffs cut below the ankle; left out.
Bukhari 1838 (a woman in ihram does not wear niqab or gloves): confirm number.
Bukhari 1545 (the Prophet set out wearing an izar and a rida'): listed as background for 'two cloths'; confirm number.
'Some pilgrims say the two white cloths remind them of a shroud': general, unsourced color; check it's fair.
Women's clothing in ihram: 'whatever color' is a simplification; some schools discourage certain dyes. Keeper to check.
Ihram as a state entered with intention (niyyah) at the miqat: general description; confirm.
Editor: dropped 'in whatever color' from women's ihram clothing (some schools discourage certain dyes).
